Word Like Fire
wûrd līk fīr
n. phrase (Jeremiah's figure for the word of God as fire and as a hammer)
Jeremiah's two similes stand in one verse: fire, which consumes and cannot be held, and a hammer that breaks rock. Both are answers to prophets who were preaching dreams.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

“Is not my word like as a fire? saith the LORD; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?” (Jer 23:29) — spoken against prophets who said, I have dreamed. The prophet knows the fire personally: “then I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name. But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay” (Jer 20:9). The Emmaus disciples felt the same heat: “Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?” (Luk 24:32). Hebrews states it without figure: the word of God is “quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword” (Heb 4:12).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines fire as heat and light emanating visibly from any body; and figuratively ardor of passion, vehemence, and the fire of the divine word; a hammer as an instrument for driving nails and beating metals.

expand to see more

FIRE, n. Heat and light emanating visibly, perceptibly and simultaneously from any body.

2. The burning of fuel on a hearth, or in any other place.

3. Ardor of passion; vehemence; animation; as the fire of zeal.

HAMMER, n. An instrument for driving nails, beating metals, and the like.

Key Scripture

Jer 23:29 — "Is not my word like as a fire? saith the LORD; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?"

Jer 20:9 — "Then I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name. But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay."

Luk 24:32 — "And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?"

Heb 4:12 — "For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart."

Jer 23:28 — "The prophet that hath a dream, let him tell a dream; and he that hath my word, let him speak my word faithfully. What is the chaff to the wheat? saith the LORD."

Modern Corruption

The word's power is sought in the preacher's heat, and Jeremiah's fire is in the word whether the preacher is warm or not.

expand to see more

The verse before the figure sets up its point exactly: “The prophet that hath a dream, let him tell a dream; and he that hath my word, let him speak my word faithfully. What is the chaff to the wheat?” (Jer 23:28). The contrast is between men supplying their own material and men delivering God's, and the fire belongs to the second regardless of the temperature of the man carrying it. A preacher who tries to supply the heat himself has become one of the dreamers; his business is faithful delivery, and the burning is the word's property.

Jeremiah 20:9 is the other side and it is the loneliest verse in the prophets. He had resolved to stop — the mockery had become unbearable — and found he could not, because the word was a fire shut up in his bones and forbearing was worse than speaking. That is the experience of a genuine call, and it is nothing like enthusiasm; it is the inability to be quiet by a man who would very much prefer to be. Any minister deciding whether to continue should read the verse before he reads a survey.

The hammer is the half usually dropped, and it says something the fire does not. Fire consumes what will burn; a hammer works on what will not. The word deals with the combustible heart and with the rock, and both are broken, and neither is left as it was. Luke 24:32 is what it feels like when the fire does its work on a believer, and Acts 2:37 — pricked in their heart — is what the hammer feels like on a rock.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew esh (H784), fire; pattish (H6360), a hammer; dabar (H1697), word; Greek zon (G2198) and energes (G1756), quick and powerful.

expand to see more

Hebrew esh (H784) — fire; Jeremiah 23:29, 20:9, Deuteronomy 4:24, Hebrews 12:29.

Hebrew pattish (H6360) — hammer; Jeremiah 23:29, 50:23, Isaiah 41:7.

Greek energes (G1756) — powerful, active; Hebrews 4:12, 1 Corinthians 16:9, Philemon 1:6.

Usage

"“Is not my word like as a fire?… and like a hammer” — two tools, and the second is usually dropped."

"“A burning fire shut up in my bones” — a man who wanted to stop and could not."

"“What is the chaff to the wheat?” — the verse before the figure."
